An internally vertex-disjoint $T$-path system is accompanied by $X\\subseteq V\\setminus T$ and a partition $\\mathcal{Y}$ of $V\\setminus(T\\cup X)$. For each $Y\\in\\mathcal{Y}$, define\n\n$$\nB_Y=\\\\{v\\in Y: v\\text{ has a neighbour in }V\\setminus(X\\cup Y)\\\\}.\n$$\n\nAfter deleting $X$ and all edges inside the parts $Y$, no $T$-path remains; the paths cover $X$ and all but at most one vertex of each $B_Y$. Each path either meets $X$ once and each $B_Y$ at most once, or meets $X$ not at all, meets one uniquely determined $B_Y$ twice, and every other $B_Y$ at most once; moreover, at most one path meets each $B_Y$ exactly once.\n\n**Mader's internally-disjoint-path conjecture.** Such a system $\\mathcal{P}$, set $X$, and partition $\\mathcal{Y}$ exist.\n\nThis is proposed as an infinite complementary-slackness analogue of Mader's finite minimax theorem for internally vertex-disjoint $T$-paths. For each $Y\\in\\mathcal{Y}$, define\n\n$$\nB_Y=\\\\{v\\in Y: v\\text{ has a neighbour in }V\\setminus(X\\cup Y)\\\\}.\n$$\n\nAfter deleting $X$ and all edges inside the parts $Y$, no $T$-path remains; the paths cover $X$ and all but at most one vertex of each $B_Y$. Each path either meets $X$ once and each $B_Y$ at most once, or meets $X$ not at all, meets one uniquely determined $B_Y$ twice, and every other $B_Y$ at most once; moreover, at most one path meets each $B_Y$ exactly once.\n\n**Mader's internally-disjoint-path conjecture.** Such a system $\\mathcal{P}$, set $X$, and partition $\\mathcal{Y}$ exist.\n\nThis is proposed as an infinite complementary-slackness analogue of Mader's finite minimax theorem for internally vertex-disjoint $T$-paths.
